meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Draft One Section - Diction and Precision
meta.title: Draft One: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: In a positive review of an architect's plan for a large public library, which word best expresses that the design is bold and ambitious without suggesting carelessness?
questions.explanation: Visionary conveys bold, forward-looking ambition without the negative connotations of recklessness or foolishness.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A draft states, Due to the fact that the power failed, the game was called off. Which revision is most concise while preserving the cause?
choices: The game was called off even though the power failed.
The game was called off, and the power failed afterward.
The power failed because the game was called off.
The game was called off because the power failed.
questions.explanation: The correct revision removes unnecessary words while clearly identifying the power failure as the reason the game was called off.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A final report gives a ___ account of an incident because it omits facts that might harm the institution involved. Which adjective is most precise?
questions.explanation: One-sided precisely describes an account that presents only a partial or biased perspective.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A reviewer writes, The auditor remained disinterested while comparing the two bids. Which word best explains what disinterested means in this context?
questions.explanation: Impartial means free from favoritism or bias, which matches the auditor's neutral comparison of the bids.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A critic describes an antagonist as cunning, while another description calls the character shrewd. Which word more strongly suggests clever and deceitful manipulation?
questions.explanation: Cunning carries the stronger implication of deception or manipulative intent.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: In a review, a writer calls a documentary uncompromising because it presents difficult evidence without softening or omitting it. Which phrase best explains the word in this context?
choices: unable to remain focused on a subject
questions.explanation: Uncompromising means unwilling to compromise principles or soften a difficult treatment, which matches the documentary's direct presentation of evidence.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A draft says, Because the data were so unique, the finding was unprecedented. If the data had never been observed in any earlier study, which revision expresses the intended reason most precisely?
choices: Because the data had never been observed before, the finding was unprecedented.
Because the data were unique, the finding was unprecedented.
Because the finding was unprecedented, the data were unique.
Because the data were ordinary, the finding was unprecedented.
questions.explanation: The revision defines unique as never having been observed before and connects that fact directly to the unprecedented finding.
questions.skill: Replace vague wording with exact definitions
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A reporter describes two officials whose accounts directly contradict one another and who refuse to reconcile them. Which adjective most precisely characterizes the disagreement?
questions.explanation: Irreconcilable precisely describes a disagreement that cannot be resolved because the opposing accounts will not be reconciled.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A rubric says, "Your response should contain no more than 300 words." Which term names 300 as the upper limit?
questions.explanation: Maximum means the greatest amount allowed, so 300 words is the upper limit.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A reviewer says, The scientist presented a cogent argument that the data warranted further study. What does cogent mean in this context?
questions.explanation: Cogent means logically convincing, which describes an argument supported by reasons that strongly support its conclusion.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: City engineers say that adding drainage capacity can ___ the danger of flash floods during heavy rain, although no construction can remove the risk completely. Which word most precisely means to make a danger less severe or less frequent?
questions.explanation: Mitigate means to reduce the severity or frequency of a danger without necessarily eliminating it.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A survey records the following results: 42 of 60 respondents support a proposed change, 15 oppose it, and 3 give no response. Which sentence most precisely reports the result without implying that every surveyed person supported the change?
choices: Forty-two of the 60 surveyed respondents supported the change, while 15 opposed it and 3 gave no response.
Most respondents supported the change, although some opposed it and a few did not answer.
The change received broad support, with only a minority expressing objections.
Most respondents supported the change, but opposition was not insignificant.
questions.explanation: This sentence provides the exact numbers for each response category without making an unsupported claim about the entire group.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: An independent review repeats earlier data and provides additional support for its accuracy. Which verb most precisely describes this relationship?
questions.explanation: To corroborate information is to support its accuracy or reliability by providing independent evidence.
questions.skill: Choosing a verb that states the exact relationship
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Residents report that construction noise and a blocked sidewalk regularly interfere with their routines, although the project has not caused injuries or serious hazards. Which noun most precisely describes the project's effect on them?
questions.explanation: A nuisance is a troublesome inconvenience, whereas the other terms suggest greater danger or severity than the situation described.
questions.skill: Choose words whose connotations match the context
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt:
Which revision of the sentence is most concise while preserving the original meaning?
Original: At the present time, the library is temporarily closed because repairs are being made.
choices: The library is temporarily closed while repairs are being made.
The library is closed for temporary repairs.
The library is temporarily closed for repairs.
At present, the library is closed temporarily because repairs are being made.
questions.explanation: The library is temporarily closed for repairs preserves the original meaning in the fewest words.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A historian uses several firsthand accounts to support a claim about a past event while acknowledging that the surviving records are incomplete. Which noun most precisely names the role of those accounts?
questions.explanation: The accounts are evidence supporting the historian's claim but not proof that eliminates every possible doubt.
questions.skill: Distinguish supporting information from stronger claims
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A technician's report states that the engineer ___ a damaged support beam by sealing its cracks and restoring its strength. Which verb is most precise?
questions.explanation: Repaired precisely describes restoring a damaged component to usable condition without replacing it.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: In a formal email to a university office, which sentence politely requests confirmation of a funding decision by Friday?
choices: Send me a message right now about whether you can approve the funding request by Friday.
Please confirm by Friday whether the funding request can be approved.
You must let me know if the funding request is approved by Friday, thanks.
Just get back to me ASAP about the money thing by Friday.
questions.explanation: The chosen sentence makes the request and deadline clear while maintaining a courteous professional tone.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A paragraph lists several tasks performed without care or genuine effort. Which adjective most precisely describes that quality?
questions.explanation: Perfunctory describes work performed routinely and without genuine care or interest.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A report compares two processes. The new process produced a smaller number of errors and required a smaller amount of time and effort. Which sentence expresses those facts with the most precise quantifiers?
choices: The new process produced less errors and required less time and effort.
The new process produced less errors and required fewer time and effort.
The new process produced fewer errors and required fewer time and effort.
The new process produced fewer errors and required less time and effort.
questions.explanation: Fewer correctly describes a smaller number of countable errors, while less correctly describes a smaller amount of time and effort.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A company must state plainly that it ended 400 positions through automation. Which verb is most precise and least euphemistic?
questions.explanation: Eliminated directly means removed or discontinued, making it the clearest verb for describing the loss of 400 positions.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Which revision makes explicit that the training schedule belongs to Priya?
choices: After Priya met the coach, Priya and the coach discussed their training schedules.
After Priya met the coach, she discussed her training schedule.
After Priya met the coach, they discussed her training schedule.
After Priya met the coach, they discussed Priya's training schedule.
questions.explanation: Using the possessive noun Priya's states plainly that the schedule belongs to Priya rather than leaving the reference implicit.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Which statement accurately distinguishes statistical significance from practical importance?
choices: Both statistical significance and practical importance describe the size of an effect in practical units.
Statistical significance measures an effect's real-world value, while practical importance indicates whether data provide strong evidence against a specified null hypothesis.
Statistical significance indicates whether data provide strong evidence against a specified null hypothesis, while practical importance concerns whether an effect matters in context.
Statistical significance applies only to effects that matter in context, while practical importance applies only to results with large sample sizes.
questions.explanation: Statistical significance concerns evidence against a null hypothesis, whereas practical importance concerns the effect's significance in a real context.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: An event report says many attendees left before the intermission, and the attendance log records that 126 of the 300 attendees left. Which revision is most precise?
choices: Most of the 300 attendees left before intermission.
126 of the 300 attendees left before intermission.
Only 126 people were in the intermission audience.
More than 100 of the 300 attendees left before intermission.
questions.explanation: The correct revision states the exact number of attendees who left and the total number of attendees.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: In "We rested on the bank of the stream," which meaning of bank is intended?
choices: the sloping land beside a body of water
a raised shelf inside a building
questions.explanation: The bank of a stream is the sloping land along the side of the body of water.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A company says, We are considering several possible responses to the issue. Which adjective most precisely describes this deliberately uncommitted statement?
questions.explanation: Equivocal describes language that leaves the speaker's position open to more than one interpretation.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A technician inspected a machine, replaced its damaged belt, and restored power, but the draft shifts to passive voice for the last action: The technician inspected the machine, replaced the damaged belt, and the power was restored. Which revision keeps the technician as the agent of all three actions and uses parallel verb structure?
choices: The technician inspected the machine, the belt was replaced, and power was restored.
The machine was inspected, the damaged belt was replaced, and power was restored.
After inspecting the machine and replacing the damaged belt, the technician restored power.
The technician inspected the machine, replaced the damaged belt, and restored power.
questions.explanation: The revision maintains the technician as the subject and coordinates three simple-past verbs in the same grammatical form.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses diction appropriate for a formal scientific report while preserving the stated meaning?
choices: The trial pulled in 48 people and wrote down that nobody died during follow-up.
The trial grabbed 48 participants and logged zero deaths during follow-up.
The trial enrolled 48 participants and observed no deaths during follow-up.
The trial hooked 48 participants and jotted down that no deaths occurred during follow-up.
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses precise, formal diction such as enrolled and observed without adding conversational wording.
questions.skill: Adapting diction to a scientific audience
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Which revision most clearly communicates that the pharmacist called Mateo and then the pharmacist reminded Mateo to refill the prescription?
choices: The pharmacist called Mateo and then reminded him to refill the prescription.
The pharmacist and Mateo discussed the need to refill the prescription.
The pharmacist called to tell Mateo that the prescription needed refilling.
The pharmacist called Mateo, who then reminded the pharmacist to refill the prescription.
questions.explanation: This revision preserves both the call and the later reminder while making the sequence of actions clear.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Which revision most clearly and concisely conveys that Maya both reviewed and then completed the checklist?
choices: After reviewing the checklist, it was completed by Maya.
Maya completed the checklist after reviewing it.
Having reviewed the checklist, it was completed by Maya.
The checklist was completed by Maya after a review.
questions.explanation: This active sentence clearly makes Maya the actor and preserves the order of reviewing before completing.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A critic writes that the final song was moving. Which phrase best captures the critic's likely meaning?
questions.explanation: In a review, moving describes a song that strongly affects the listener's emotions.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Two analyses use different evidence but reach the same conclusion. Which word most precisely describes the relationship between the analyses?
questions.explanation: Convergent describes separate lines of reasoning that move toward the same conclusion.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: In "The coach gave a candid response when asked about the team's chances," what does candid mean?
questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and direct, especially when giving an assessment.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: In a formal email to a university admissions office, which sentence communicates the request clearly while maintaining an appropriate professional tone?
choices: I need you to tell me what's happening with my application right away.
I request an update on the status of my application.
Could you possibly send me the thing about my application whenever convenient?
Hey, can u send me my application status?
questions.explanation: This sentence states the request directly in formal language and clearly identifies the information being requested.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A city survey found that most residents opposed the plan specifically because of its projected cost. Which sentence reports that finding in suitable formal diction?
choices: Most residents opposed the plan because of its projected cost.
Most residents rejected the plan after hearing its projected cost.
Most residents believe the plan will be costly and unpopular.
Most residents have criticized the plan's projected cost.
questions.explanation: This sentence accurately reports both the residents' opposition and its stated reason while maintaining formal diction.
questions.skill: Revise for a professional audience without changing meaning
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A spokesperson ___ reporters' questions during the press conference by giving specific details about the policy. Which verb is most precise?
questions.explanation: Answered precisely describes the spokesperson's act of responding to reporters' questions.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: After a formal review, a government permanently ends a public program that will never operate, and no replacement program is created. Which verb most precisely reports this action in a formal document?
questions.explanation: To abolish a program is to end it formally and permanently, which matches the action described.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Which word most precisely names a treatment that reduces the severity of a problem without eliminating it?
questions.explanation: A palliative measure relieves symptoms or reduces severity without curing the underlying problem.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: The coach told Andre that he had missed practice. Which interpretation of the sentence is valid?
choices: It is clear that Andre missed practice.
It is unclear whether the coach or Andre missed practice.
It is clear that the coach missed practice.
Neither the coach nor Andre missed practice.
questions.explanation: Because both the coach and Andre are plausible antecedents of he, the sentence does not establish who missed practice.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A draft says, The tutoring program helped many students improve their grades. The notes show that 23 of 40 participants raised their grades by at least 5 points, while the others did not. Which revision is most precise?
choices: The tutoring program helped 23 of 40 participants improve their grades.
Twenty-three of the 40 participants raised their grades by at least 5 points.
The tutoring program improved grades for a majority of participants.
Many participants improved their grades with help from the tutoring program.
questions.explanation: The third choice reports the exact number of participants, the total number, and the defined amount of improvement without making an unsupported causal claim.
questions.skill: Revise vague claims with precise information
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: An earthquake severely damaged buildings throughout a city, but the evidence does not show that every structure was completely destroyed. Which word most precisely describes the damage without overstating it?
questions.explanation: Devastated means severely damaged or ruined, so it accurately describes the earthquake's effects without claiming that every structure was completely destroyed.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: Which revision of "The report was written by the committee, and the committee was chaired by Elena" avoids repeating committee while using a nonessential participial phrase?
choices: The committee, chaired by Elena, wrote the report.
The report was written by a committee chaired by Elena.
Elena chaired the committee that wrote the report.
The committee wrote the report after Elena chaired it.
questions.explanation: The phrase chaired by Elena is a nonessential participial phrase that identifies Elena as the committee's chair without repeating committee.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A clinic's average wait time changed from 18 minutes before a scheduling change to 12 minutes afterward. Which statement reports the decrease accurately?
choices: Average wait time decreased by 6 minutes.
Average wait time decreased by 18 minutes.
Average wait time decreased by 12 minutes.
Average wait time decreased by 6 percent.
questions.explanation: The wait time fell from 18 minutes to 12 minutes, a decrease of 6 minutes.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: In a review, "The violin soloist gave a striking performance, surprising the audience with several bold improvisations." What does striking mean in this context?
choices: unusual only because it broke written rules
questions.explanation: Striking means remarkable or attention-grabbing, which fits a performance that surprised the audience.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A confidential source asks a reporter not to publish their name because they fear retaliation. Which word most precisely names the condition of remaining unnamed?
questions.explanation: Anonymity specifically refers to the condition of being unnamed or unidentified.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: In a methods section, which noun phrase most precisely identifies genetic material from another organism that has entered a DNA sample?
questions.explanation: DNA contamination names unwanted genetic material introduced from another organism into a sample.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A disease appears at irregular intervals in a community, with a few cases scattered across several months. Which adjective most precisely describes this pattern?
questions.explanation: Sporadic means occurring occasionally and at irregular intervals.
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A supervisor says, The presentation was fine, meaning that it met every criterion on the rubric. Which revision is most precise?
choices: The presentation met every criterion on the rubric.
The presentation was good enough for approval.
questions.explanation: The revision states the evaluative standard directly instead of substituting vague praise such as fine.
questions.skill: Replacing vague language with exact wording
questions.topic: Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A critic wants to praise a performance as imaginative and innovative without exaggerating its historical impact or using slang. Which phrase is most precise and appropriate?
questions.explanation: Highly inventive praises creative work directly without overstating its broader impact or relying on exaggerated slang.
questions.topic: Draft One Section - Diction and Precision

questions.prompt: A draft says, The manager sent Priya the report because she needed it. The intended meaning is that Priya needed the report to complete her work. Which revision removes the pronoun's ambiguity?
choices: The manager sent Priya the report because she was the manager.
The manager sent Priya the report because the manager needed it.
The manager sent Priya the report because the report was needed.
The manager sent Priya the report because Priya needed it.
questions.explanation: Repeating Priya makes clear that she, rather than the manager or the report, is the person who needed it.
questions.skill: Eliminate ambiguous references with precise wording
questions.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Draft One Section - Diction and Precision
